Concrete failure: tabs=[Tab('A','x'), Tab('A2','x'), Tab('B','y')], active 'y' -> _bar_position=2.0, displayed has 2 entries, index = 2 % 2 = 0 -> underline is drawn under the 'x' tab, not 'y'. Silent misplacement.

Reference is also wrong on this input but fails louder: find_tab_by_name over the full list (reference tabs.py:325-331) gives 2, and reference tabs.py:155 indexes range_values[2] on a 2-entry list, raising IndexError. So this is not a parity regression, but the candidate does not show the intended underline.

Right/Left navigation stalls with duplicates: activate_next_tab (tabs.py:244-247) resolves by first match, so the next duplicate maps back to the same name. Reference (reference tabs.py:260-265) has the same stall, so this is shared.
criteria.deficiency: With duplicate tab names, the underline position is computed from the full tab list (tabs.py:225, 306, 239-242) but rendered against the deduplicated list (tabs.py:76, 134-139). Example: tabs [A(x), A2(x), B(y)] with active 'y' draws the underline under 'x'. The reference raises IndexError on the same input (reference tabs.py:155), so this is a shared-design defect that the candidate fails silently. Fix would be to map the position through the deduplicated list.
